summary:
Width: an unresolved width is now 'at most' only when both ends are seen bounded by free space (cards.ends: end-region points moved past the extreme point, timeline.place on the object's own views); otherwise 'at least' the single-view median extent when resolved, else 'not observed'. On the same GT cards (TUM, ARKit x2, warm, GT cover >= 0.5) the new 'at least' bounds hold 122/124 (a, assumed 1.6 m) and 119/124 (b, true height); round 4's 'at most' held 150/158 (a) and 149/158 (b). Value coverage is unchanged (e.g. TUM 200/212 (a), 193/212 (b)). 'at most' is now rare: 1 of 158 unresolved widths had both ends free. Retail width coverage falls from 89-94 % to 32-55 %.

Time: every object card carries a timeline over its shot's content windows (ORB co-visibility 0.40, computed in the process pool beside DA3). Each window has a state (first seen / appeared / static / moved / disappeared / not observed with reason) and values measured on that window's points (+-u with a coverage term). Intervals carry pooled values. A change is flagged only when it exceeds both u's (shared scale excluded). 'moved' also needs the old place seen empty. Every claim carries evidence keyframes. Other rules:
- look-alike test: a place seen empty onto a same-word object in the pick maps is no claim.
- screen-band guard: burned-in captions get no claims.
- deformables are re-measured per window, with no place claims.
- people are placed per keyframe.
- disappeared/appeared cards of one kind are linked as moves; the better-seen card's model is posed at each place.

Viewer:
- the card shows the timeline bar, the state at the video's time, values per interval, changes with evidence, and per-window rows.
- the objects list shows each card's state at t, with a 'with a change' filter.
- changed cards are drawn per interval in 3D; people get a marker per keyframe.
- screenshots were captured and asserted in web/tests/r5b-time-shots.mjs.

Evaluation:
- 0 claims on real footage: 8 retail calls (5,239 cards) and 6 static GT calls (799 cards; 1,502 unseen windows judged occupied, 0 free).
- Planted events (r5b plants with before and after both seen, plus X6's plants): 5 of 9 claimed.
- 10 claims on planted clips: 7 true, 3 false. All 3 false claims are on planted Walmart boxes, where depth drift splits one static box into 2-5 cards along the aisle.
- 1 of 2 move links names the wrong source.
- Real moves (agent-labelled): 0 of 2.

Added cost: timeline 1.8-9.8 CPU-s and ends 1.1-3.6 CPU-s per cards build over 24 processes. Cards stages differ on vs off by -1.8 to +2.7 s. Walmart's clean pair adds +1.7 and +3.5 s at cards v3 (target <= +5 s met on these). ME340 and Sam's Club milestone differences are dominated by vocabulary variance.

summary:
I built cross-visit analysis in fast_report/visits.py. A new visit's video is registered into the first visit's site map, its objects are matched to the site map's, identities / names / display models carry over, and the differences go into a `visits` layer. The live viewer shows that layer in a new Visits tab (web/src/VisitsPanel.tsx): you pick visit A and/or B, changed objects are coloured, the site map's missing objects appear as ghosts, and each change opens its evidence frame.

How it works:
- **Registration:** DINOv2 picks matching keyframes, one DA3 any-view pass runs on about 30 frames, and a Sim3 fit uses register_cut_shot's gate. The scale comes from either the depth ratio or the camera centres, whichever puts the new visit's floor closer to the site map's. Views that fit badly are dropped and the fit is redone, then it is snapped to the floors so heights compare directly.
- **Matching:** position, type, DINOv2 appearance, and the two objects must share a volume (grown by the registration u).
- **Changes:** a see-through test on the other visit's depth decides missing / new / moved; height changes need the missing part to be seen through. Places the other visit never saw clearly are 'not observed', never missing.

Results against ground truth (TUM fr1 all share one mocap frame; the two ARKit sessions were aligned by ICP of their LiDAR):
- **Registration:** 4.9-12.0 cm median error and 0.7-3.0 deg on every accepted shot. The reported u covers the GT error on 7 of 14 registrations and 2u covers all 14.
- **Refused registrations:** the same-session ARKit window (0.106 against the gate's 0.1) and 6 of the 7 short shots of the 360 sequence.
- **Object match:** precision 0.70 pooled (0.51-0.81 per pair), recall 0.76 pooled (0.86-1.00 where shots registered).
- **Change claims:** 17 in all, 13 right, 3 wrong, 1 unclear, so precision 0.81. The right ones are real rearrangements between TUM recordings: a chair moved 2.5 m, a notepad gone in two recordings, a monitor, chair, jacket, mouse and small boxes new.
- **False changes:** 3 wrong claims on 1,660 judged objects (0.18 %). On our own clip the 3 claims are all the filmer's own cart, which moves with the camera.
- **Change recall is low:** 10 of the 137 changes GT sees (5 of 83 for objects 30 cm or larger). With 5-12 cm registration and estimated depth, a place only reads empty when the background is well behind the object. Looser margins found more changes on TUM but added false claims on our clip, so I kept X6's rule.
- **Heights and angles:** 55 height differences were measured but none confirmed by the see-through test, and no angle difference was measured on both visits, so there are no height or angle claims.

Time on 2x A100: a revisit analysed with its visit step committed the visits layer 56-99 s after its MP4 arrived. The visit stage itself took 10.9-17.3 s, and a standalone FastReport.visit call takes 5.7-17.4 s to commit (median 10.0 s). GPU peaks stayed at or below 67.1 GiB.

In all my runs, event captions were off, the vocabulary prompt had no safety list, judgement was off, and the shared naming bank was not written to.

issues: Change recall is low: 10 of 137 GT changes found (5 of 83 for objects 30 cm or larger). With 5-12 cm registration and estimated depth, things lying on desks or against walls stay 'occupied'. Relaxed see-through margins (calibrated on 4,020 TUM cards) doubled recall but added false claims on static shelves in our Sam's Club clip. A check comparing the other visit's crop at the projected place with the object's own crop is the next thing to try; it is untried.

Object match precision is 0.51-0.81 per pair: neighbours that look alike get swapped under the registration error. It is worst on plant and teddy, where the camera height and viewpoints differ most. The shared-volume gate raised pooled precision from 0.64 to 0.75 in development (0.70 on the final layers).

Registration refused: the same-session ARKit window 47333932 w1 (0.106 against the gate's 0.1) and 6 of 7 cut-short shots of TUM 360. Objects in a refused shot are 'not compared'. There is one site map per site (the first visit), and each revisit shot is registered to only one site-map shot.
The reported registration u covers the GT error at 1u on only 7 of 14 registrations (all 14 at 2u).
The filmer's own shopping cart in Sam's Club moves with the camera and shows up as real moved / new / missing claims. A within-video rule marking objects carried by the camera would drop it.
No angle change was ever measured on both visits, so the changed-angle path is exercised only by its self-check; there is no GT for angles here.
The comparison's CPU part (lifting objects and see-through tests) runs on one thread: 4-12 s per revisit, 12 s on Sam's Club. A thread pool over objects would cut it.
web/tests/live-report-check.ts needs runs/fb-c-fixture-001, which is no longer on disk. Its synthetic part passes and tsc passes.
These analyses ran with event captions off, the vocabulary prompt without its safety list, judgement off, and the bank not saved, so their object layers do not use r4b's settings.

Local disk dropped to about 4 GB during the round while other builders were writing (below the 8 GB pull limit).
